claims.text: Limited interfacial heat transfer primarily governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or nanoribbons under low-field cycling.
The as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi material has inherent structural heterogeneities.
The as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi material exhibits intrinsic magnetic-domain behavior relevant to its response.
A 5–10 nm AlN cap is the controlled intervention to be compared with an uncapped as-deposited baseline.
AlN is a high-thermal-conductivity cap material in the proposed nanoscale configuration.
Adding the AlN cap enhances interfacial thermal conductance between the FeMnNiGeSi alloy and its environment.
Enhanced interfacial thermal conductance reduces the effective thermal resistance experienced by the alloy during cycling.
The AlN cap promotes faster and more spatially uniform temperature equilibration during cooling cycles.
Faster heat extraction minimizes thermal gradients and thermal lag in the magnetostructural transition.
Minimizing thermal gradients and transition delay sharpens the magnetostructural transition.
Faster and more uniform equilibration reduces hysteresis.
The AlN-capped samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change per cycle than uncapped samples.
The AlN-capped samples will exhibit a smaller hysteresis-loop area than uncapped samples.
The predicted benefits of the cap should become more evident toward the higher end of the 0.5–2 Hz cycling range.
Uncapped as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons typically have broader hysteresis than capped samples under comparable low-field, low-frequency conditions.
Uncapped as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons typically have lower magnetocaloric performance than capped samples under comparable conditions.
The proposed mechanism is applicable at applied fields below 100 Oe, cycling frequencies of 0.5–2 Hz, and ambient temperature.
Mechanical strain or interfacial chemistry introduced by the cap could independently alter the magnetic properties.
